brief: While the major hyperscalers have raised AI capital spending roughly 6-9x since 2023, Apple has kept capex flat, now below pre-AI-boom levels; capex as a share of sales has doubled or tripled for the hyperscalers while falling by about a third for Apple. The market is rewarding that restraint rather than punishing it: Apple is the only Magnificent Seven stock beating both the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 year-to-date, up 25%, and has decoupled from the Nasdaq. Apple trades at roughly 36x forward earnings, a 17-point premium to the S&P 500, which the note frames as the market's reward for sitting out the AI spending race rather than falling behind in it. Analyst sentiment lags the share performance: only 57% of analysts are buy/overweight on Apple, versus over 90% for Nvidia at its peak. The publisher reiterates its long-Apple, anti-AI trade call made weeks earlier, saying it continues to perform well, beating the Nasdaq 100 and beating by an even wider margin when expressed against Nvidia.
